cloze.title: 原文选词填空
cloze.instruction: 从词库中选择合适的词填入空白，每词使用一次，保留原文词形。大小写不影响判分。

parts.text: Although the Every Student Succeeds Act aimed to reduce the role of testing in classrooms, standardized tests continue to

what teachers teach, how they use instructional time and how schools define success.

All U.S. public schools are required to administer standardized tests in reading and math annually to students in grades three through eight and at least once in high

. These tests measure whether students are reading and understanding mathematics at, above or below the average, when compared to other students across the state.

Students’ scores on these tests can affect schools’ ratings and

, and can also determine whether states monitor or take over public school districts that are not performing well.

Too much time

The exact number of tests students take each year before high school ranges from 35 to 88 tests. The study also found no relationship between the number of

students took and their proficiency or growth in English or mathematics.

The National Association of State Boards of Education also reports that some districts give students seven assessments per grade, with most tests administered one to three times a year.

Older research also

the time teachers spend preparing students for state tests.

A 2016 survey found that 62% of K-12 public school teachers reported spending too much time preparing students for state-mandated tests. Teachers
spending an average of 14 out of 180 school days preparing students for these exams, whether it be reviewing the question

students see on tests or teaching test-taking strategies.

In the same 2016 national survey, 29% of teachers reported spending more than a month preparing students in grades K-12 for state-mandated tests.

Costly in other ways

Teachers also feel the effects of spending so much time preparing students for standardized tests.

Research on teacher

has found that teachers’ dissatisfaction with standardized testing was a key reason they left the profession.

Other research from 2026 found that teachers who worried about job consequences tied to test results reported lower job

.

These numbers tell a larger story. The costs of standardized testing do not simply appear in the amount printed on contracts with testing companies.

They are also reflected in lesson plans, teachers’ workloads, classroom time, professional
and the opportunities that disappear when preparing for a test becomes a central purpose of schooling.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Schools can reduce some learning gaps while advantages linked to family wealth persist.
A heavy burden of standardised testing does not necessarily lead to better learning.
School recess supports children's development in ways that extend beyond entertainment.
Minority language speakers continue to face prejudice in different European settings.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: The costs of standardized testing do not simply appear in the amount printed on contracts with testing companies.

questions.prompt: What change in teaching time followed expanded testing in many school districts?
options: Time spent on every subject increased by exactly the same amount.
All English and mathematics teaching was eliminated.
School districts stopped teaching tested content.
Weekly English and mathematics time increased.
questions.explanation: 第 4 段提供了作答依据。正确选项用不同说法表达了文中的信息；请比较范围、数量、因果关系与限定词。
questions.evidence: Many school districts increased their instructional weekly time for English and mathematics, with average increases of 47% for English and 37% for mathematics from 2001 to 2007.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is explicitly made in paragraph 10?
options: The study also found no relationship between the number of assessments students took and their proficiency or growth in English or mathematics.
The costs of standardized testing do not simply appear in the amount printed on contracts with testing companies.
The public K-12 school system in the United States has become pervasively shaped by standardized testing.
All U.S. public schools are required to administer standardized tests in reading and math annually to students in grades three through eight and at least once in high school.
questions.explanation: 定位第 10 段，比较四个选项的具体信息。其余选项来自本文其他段落，并非本段明确陈述的内容。
questions.evidence: All U.S. public schools are required to administer standardized tests in reading and math annually to students in grades three through eight and at least once in high school.
